strengths: The authors propose certain modifications to the initialization steps prior to optimizing 3D Gaussian splatting representations. It leads to small but consistent improvements in the reconstruction quality on several datasets especially when the optimizer is started with noisy or random initialization of the 3D point coordinates. In general, the arguments and insights they present sounds reasonable in theory and seems to be helping in practice as shown in the empirical results.
The proposed method is simple to add to the existing 3DGS method
The authors provide exhaustive experiments to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method
The proposed method improves the original 3DGS clearly on the tanks-and-temples and the MipNeRF360 dataset.
This paper proposes to reconstruct Gaussian scenes using randomly initialized point clouds. In some cases, the proposed method surpasses Colmap+3DGS, which is impressive.
The proposed method encourages Gaussian scenes to first learn global structural information before focusing on detailed information.
The analysis in this paper is well-organized and clearly written.

Significance. Relaxing the initialization constraint of 3DGS is a critical and meaningful problem. The RAIN-GS realizes an impressive performance without the need of SfM points, proving it is an efficient solution.
weaknesses: The authors try to improve 3DGS performance when the Gaussians are initialized from random 3D points, but they assume that the camera poses are accurate; a full SfM pipeline with bundle adjustment would already provide accurate points, so there is little compelling situation for random initialization when accurate poses are available.

The main paper lacks sufficient technical detail; the idea of limited Gaussian portability is presented with an empirical study on the Mip-NeRF360 dataset but without deeper insights, and the claimed first contribution appears not to extend beyond existing literature on local minima.

The modifications to initialization do not guarantee escaping local minima; claims should be toned down, and the ABE-Split heuristic is a variation of existing strategies with little justification for its specific criteria.
The ideas are intuitive and the contributions are not significant.
It is unclear whether the same strategies would improve other variants of 3DGS such as scaffold-gs.
The method’s effectiveness on texture-less areas is not demonstrated; the reviewer would like to see results on such regions.
The design mainly comes from experimental results; it lacks theoretical novelty, many hyperparameters require tuning, and more detailed ablation experiments on these hyperparameters are needed.

The paper assumes known multi-view image poses without point cloud reconstruction, but further analysis is needed regarding pose errors, robustness to pose inaccuracies, and validation on images generated from generative models.

The submission only includes 3DGS and Mip-Splatting for comparison, which is unreasonable for ICLR; comparisons should include methods like ScaffoldGS or other recent improvements that are randomly initialized.
It remains unclear where RAIN-GS’s improvement comes from; the authors should compare their method in both Table 2 and Figure 2 to validate the motivation and effectiveness of their method.
